title: Global Post-Death Civil Registration & Estate Administration Atlas (2026)

registrationWindowDistribution.label: Automatic digital registration
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Attending physician or hospital transmits an electronic medical notice directly into the national civil/population register, removing a separate family registry visit.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: Within 48 hours / next working day
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Statutory civil registration is coupled tightly with sanitary burial or cremation clearance, so filings occur within 12 to 48 hours.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: 3 to 7 days
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Allows several working days after medical certification (or after burial/cremation in countries like New Zealand) for families or funeral directors to file.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: 8 to 35 days (up to 1 month)
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Accommodates larger territorial distances, commune/district reporting chains, or family travel before civil registration fees apply.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: 6 weeks to 12 months
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Provides extended statutory free-registration windows (6 weeks to 12 months) while medical or municipal burial orders still govern immediate interment.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: Prior to burial / prompt statutory filing
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Statute requires registration promptly or prior to the municipal burial/cremation order without prescribing a uniform nationwide day count.

registrationWindowDistribution.label: Sub-national (state, provincial, or emirate)
registrationWindowDistribution.description: Constitutional division allocates vital-statistics deadlines to states, provinces, emirates, or autonomous island states rather than one federal statute.

filingChannelDistribution.label: Electronic health feed or national e-portal
filingChannelDistribution.description: Physicians, hospitals, or citizens submit death notices electronically through interconnected health-to-registry platforms or national e-government portals.

filingChannelDistribution.label: Funeral director or care facility intermediary
filingChannelDistribution.description: Licensed funeral directors or hospital administrations routinely submit the formal declaration to the civil registrar on behalf of the bereaved family.

filingChannelDistribution.label: In-person family or local informant
filingChannelDistribution.description: A surviving relative or statutory informant typically attends a municipal, district, or civil registry counter in person with paper medical proof.

agencyPropagationDistribution.label: Automated register propagation or one-stop desk
agencyPropagationDistribution.description: Civil registration triggers automatic population-register broadcasts to tax, pension, or social-insurance agencies, or provides a consolidated government Tell-Us-Once desk.

agencyPropagationDistribution.label: Manual agency-by-agency notifications
agencyPropagationDistribution.description: Families must carry certified death certificates separately to social security funds, pension offices, tax authorities, and banks to stop benefits and open claims.

estateGatekeeperDistribution.label: Civil-law notary / extrajudicial deed
estateGatekeeperDistribution.description: Public or sworn notaries issue certificates of heirship, execute extrajudicial partitions (when adult heirs agree), and search national will registers.

estateGatekeeperDistribution.label: Common-law probate court / Master of High Court
estateGatekeeperDistribution.description: Executors apply to High Court / Supreme Court Probate Registries (or the Master of the High Court) for a Grant of Probate or Letters of Administration.

estateGatekeeperDistribution.label: Civil court heirship decree or statutory registry
estateGatekeeperDistribution.description: Judicial succession declarations, municipal/tax estate inventories (such as Scandinavian bouppteckning / perunkirjoitus), or administrative succession desks establish heirship.

estateGatekeeperDistribution.label: Personal-status / Sharia court or plural legal system
estateGatekeeperDistribution.description: Heirship determination (such as Hasr al-Waratha or Faraid certificates) flows through Sharia, confessional, or community-specific personal-law courts.

estateGatekeeperDistribution.label: Ex-officio court or court-commissioner initiation
estateGatekeeperDistribution.description: Once civil registration occurs, the registrar transmits the death record directly to the district probate court, which initiates succession without a family petition.

apostilleDistribution.label: 1961 Hague Apostille Convention in force (November 2026)
apostilleDistribution.description: Death certificates and probate grants circulate with a single Apostille stamp across fellow contracting states.

apostilleDistribution.label: Acceded 30 June 2026; enters into force 28 February 2027
apostilleDistribution.description: Thailand acceded on 30 June 2026; consular legalization applies until entry into force on 28 February 2027.

apostilleDistribution.label: Non-party: MFA & embassy consular legalization required
apostilleDistribution.description: Cross-border death and estate records still require multi-step Foreign Ministry and destination embassy legalization unless bilaterally exempt.
